(p-179)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah al-Jathiyah (The Kneeling)
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ ﴿And in your creation and what He spreads of living creatures are signs for a people who are certain.﴾ ﴿And the alternation of the night and the day, and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and He revives thereby the earth after its death, and the turning of the winds are signs for a people who reason.﴾

He, exalted is He and high is He, mentioned in these noble verses, from the beginning of the surah "al-Jathiyah," six proofs of monotheism, indicating His greatness and majesty, the perfection of His power, and that He alone is deserving of worship, exalted is He.

The first of them: His creation of the heavens and the earth.
The second: His creation of mankind.
The third: His creation of the living creatures.
The fourth: the alternation of the night and the day.
The fifth: the sending down of water from the sky and the reviving of the earth by it.
The sixth: the turning of the winds.

He mentioned that these signs and proofs are only benefited by the believers who are certain, who understand from Allah His proofs and signs; so it is as if they are the ones specially addressed by them, to the exclusion of others.

Therefore He said: ﴿signs for the believers﴾, then He said: ﴿signs for a people who are certain﴾, then He said: ﴿signs for a people who reason﴾.

These six proofs mentioned at the beginning of this noble surah have come clarified in very many verses, as is well known.

(p-180) As for the first of them, which is His creation of the heavens and the earth, mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, it has come in many verses,

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no rifts? And the earth — We spread it out and cast therein firm mountains and caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair, as an insight and reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾ [Qaf: 6-8].
• And His saying: ﴿Have they not seen what is before them and behind them of the sky and the earth?﴾ — the verse [Saba: 9].
• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth. But signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe."﴾ — the verse [Yunus: 101].
• And His saying: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ — the verse [al-A'raf: 158].
• And His saying: ﴿And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Rum: 22] in "al-Rum" and in "al-Shura" [al-Shura: 29].
• And His saying: ﴿He who made for you the earth a bed and the sky a building﴾ [Ghafir: 64].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the One who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a building﴾ [Ghafir: 64].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the sky We built with strength, and indeed, We are expanding it. And the earth — We spread it out, and how excellent are the spreaders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47-48].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting place?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And We built above you seven strong [heavens]﴾ [al-Naba: 6-12].

Verses similar to these are very many and well known.

As for the second of them, which is His creation of mankind, mentioned in His saying: ﴿And in your creation﴾, it has come clarified in many verses,

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, behold, you are human beings dispersing﴾ [al-Rum: 20].
• And His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾ — the verse [al-Baqarah: 21].
• And His saying, exalted is He, concerning His prophet Nuh: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not attribute to Allah due grandeur, while He has created you in stages?﴾ [Nuh: 13-14].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He creates you within the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you diverted?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6].
• And His saying: ﴿And in yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 21].

Verses similar to these are very many and well known.

As for the third of them, which is His creation of the living creatures, mentioned in His saying: ﴿and what He spreads of living creatures﴾, it has also come clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Shura": ﴿And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He has dispersed therein of living creatures; and He is, when He wills, over their gathering, competent﴾ [al-Shura: 29].
• And His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Baqarah": ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of water and He revives thereby the earth after its death and disperses therein every kind of living creature﴾ — the verse [al-Baqarah: 164].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has created every creature from water. Of them are those that walk on their bellies, and of them are those that walk on two legs, and of them are those that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Nur: 45].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle eight mates﴾ [al-Zumar: 6].

Verses similar to these are very many and well known.

As for the fourth of them, which is the alternation of the night and the day, mentioned in His saying: "and the alternation of the night and the day", it has also come clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Baqarah": ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164].
• And His saying, exalted is He, in "Al 'Imran": ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190].
• And His saying, exalted is He, in "Fussilat": ﴿And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon﴾ — the verse [Fussilat: 37].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day, and at once they are in darkness. And the sun runs to its determined place﴾ — the verse [Ya-Sin: 37-38].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have sight﴾ [al-Nur: 44].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if Allah made for you the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you light? Then will you not listen?" Say, "Have you considered: if Allah made for you the day perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you rest? Then will you not see?" And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas: 71-73].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of the night and the day. Then will you not reason?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 80].

Verses similar to these are very many and well known.

As for the fifth of them, which is the sending down of water from the sky, the reviving of the earth by it, and the growing of provision therein, mentioned in His saying: ﴿and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and He revives thereby the earth after its death﴾, it has also come clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Baqarah": ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people and what Allah sends down from the sky of water and He revives thereby the earth after its death﴾ up to His saying: ﴿are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then let mankind look at his food: that We poured down water in torrents, then We split the earth in splitting, and caused to grow therein grain and grapes﴾ up to His saying: ﴿as provision for you and your livestock﴾ [Abasa: 24-32].

(p-182) The explanation of this proof in brief is that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿let mankind look at his food﴾ is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to every accountable person to look and reflect upon his food, such as the bread by which he eats and lives, from the creation of the water which was the cause of its growth.

Can anyone other than Allah create it?
The answer: No.

Then suppose the water has been created in fact; can anyone other than Allah send it down to the earth in this manner by which benefit is obtained without harm, by sending it down upon the earth as a small spray, so that the earth is watered by it gradually, without any destruction or drowning occurring by it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿you see the rain coming out from within it﴾ [al-Nur: 43]?
The answer: No.

Then suppose the water has been created and sent down into the earth in that complete and most perfect manner; can anyone other than Allah split the earth and bring out from it the shoot of the plant?
The answer: No.

Then suppose the plant has come out of the earth and split open from it; can anyone other than Allah bring out the ear from that plant?
The answer: No.

Then suppose the ear has come out of the plant; can anyone other than Allah cause its grain to grow and carry it from stage to stage until it ripens and becomes fit for food and sustenance?
The answer: No.

And He, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-An'am: 99]. And like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent down from the rain-laden clouds water pouring forth, that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation, and gardens of dense growth﴾ [al-Naba: 14-16]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth; We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat﴾ [Ya-Sin: 33]. Verses similar to these are very many and well known.

(p-183) Know that His, exalted is He, application of the word "provision" to water in this verse of "al-Jathiyah" — we have explained its meaning in the surah "al-Mu'min" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He is the One who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ — the verse [Ghafir: 13].

As for the sixth of them, which is the turning of the winds, mentioned in His saying: ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾, it has also come clarified in verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His saying in "al-Baqarah": ﴿and the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good news﴾ [al-Rum: 46].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ [al-Hijr: 22].

And other than that of the verses.

Admonition
Know that these great proofs mentioned at the beginning of this "al-Jathiyah" — three of them are among the proofs of the Resurrection, which the Qur'an, the Mighty, frequently uses as evidence for the Resurrection, in a widespread abundance.

We have explained them in places in this blessed book, in "al-Baqarah," "al-Nahl," and others, and we have referred to them many times in this blessed book, and we will restate a portion of them here for their importance, God willing, exalted is He.

The first of the proofs mentioned is the creation of the heavens and the earth, mentioned here in this "al-Jathiyah": ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, because His, exalted and high is He, creation of the heavens and the earth is among the greatest proofs of the resurrection of people after death; for whoever created the greatest and largest, there is no doubt of His capability to create the weakest and smallest.

The verses indicating this are many:

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57], meaning: whoever is able to create the greatest, there is no doubt that He is able to create the smallest;
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Knowing Creator﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81].
• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not exhausted by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 33].
• And His saying, exalted is He: (p-184) ﴿Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is competent to create the likes of them?﴾ — the verse [al-Isra: 99]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the sky? He built it; He raised its ceiling and made it level, and darkened its night and brought out its brightness. And the earth after that He spread out; He brought out from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly, as provision for you and your livestock﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27-33].

The counterpart of this verse of "al-Nazi'at" is His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of "al-Saffat": ﴿So ask them: are they more difficult in creation or those We have created?﴾ — the verse [al-Saffat: 11]; because His saying, "those We have created," refers by it to the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is mentioned with them, which is mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them and Lord of the easts﴾ up to His saying ﴿then a piercing flame followed him﴾ [al-Saffat: 5-10].

As for the second of the proofs mentioned: it is His, exalted is He, creation of mankind the first time; for whoever originated their creation without a previous pattern, there is no doubt of His capability to re-create them a second time, as is not hidden.

The argument from this proof for the Resurrection is very frequent in the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], and so on to the end of the verses.

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78-79].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?"﴾ ﴿Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?﴾ ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils﴾, the verse [Maryam: 66-68].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾, the verse [al-Rum: 27].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who brought you forth the first time."﴾ [al-Isra': 51].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it - a promise upon Us. Indeed, We will be doing it.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Were We incapable with the first creation? Rather, they are in confusion about a new creation.﴾ [Qaf: 15].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you have already known the first creation, so why do you not remember?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 56:62].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that He created the two mates, the male and the female, from a sperm-drop when it is emitted, and that upon Him is the final creation [al-nash'ah al-ukhra]﴾ [al-Najm: 45-47].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected? ﴿Was he not a sperm-drop emitted? ﴿Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned, ﴿and made of him two mates, the male and the female. ﴿Is not that One able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 36-40].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinin, and this secure city: We have certainly created man in the best of stature,﴾ up to His saying: ﴿So what causes you to deny the Recompense after this?﴾ [al-Tin: 1-7].

Meaning: what compels you to deny the Recompense - that is, the Resurrection and the reckoning - and you know that I created you in the first creation in the best of stature. And you know that it is not hidden from any intelligent person that He who originated the first bringing into existence is beyond doubt capable of repeating it a second time. And other verses besides these.

As for the third proof among them, which is the giving of life to the earth after its death, mentioned in His saying, exalted is He, in the surah "al-Jathiyah": ﴿And what Allah sends down from the sky of provision, and with it He gives life to the earth after its death﴾, this proof is also much cited in the Glorious Qur'an for the Resurrection, because He who gives life to the earth after its death is capable of giving life to people after their death, since all are living after death.

Among the verses indicating this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is the Giver of life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.﴾ [Fussilat: 39]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it water, it stirs and swells and grows from every beautiful pair. That is because Allah is the Truth, and it is He who gives life to the dead, and it is He who is over all things competent. And that the Hour is coming, no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.﴾ [al-Hajj: 5-7]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So look at the effects of the mercy of Allah - how He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed, that is the Giver of life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.﴾ [al-Rum: 50]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water therefrom and bring out thereby fruits of all kinds. Thus will We bring out the dead; perhaps you will remember.﴾ [al-A'raf: 57].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thus will We bring out the dead﴾ means: We will resurrect them from their graves alive, just as We brought out those fruits after their non-existence, and by bringing them out We gave life to that dead land. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus you will be brought out﴾ [al-Rum: 19] means: you will be brought out from your graves alive after death. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave life thereby to a dead land. Thus is the coming out﴾ [Qaf: 11]. And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿These are the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾.

Exalted is He, pointed out to His Prophet ﷺ the signs of this Great Qur'an, and He made clear to His Prophet that He recites them to him clothed in the truth, to which falsehood does not come from before it or from behind it.

(p-186) What He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse of "al-Jathiyah" He mentioned in other verses with the same wording, such as His saying in "al-Baqarah": ﴿And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds﴾ ﴿These are the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 251-252]. And His saying in "Al 'Imran": ﴿As for those whose faces will be whitened, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide forever﴾ ﴿These are the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth; and Allah does not want injustice for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 107-108]. And His saying in this noble verse: "tilka" (these) means "hadhihi" (this).

Among the idioms of the Arabic language is the use of the demonstrative for the distant to refer to the near, as in His saying: ﴿Dhalika al-Kitab﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2], meaning "this Book", as al-Bukhari related it from Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna. Among its evidences is the verse of Khufaf ibn Nadbah al-Sulami:

"If my horses have been struck at their core, then deliberately I aimed at Malik with my eye.
I say to him while the spear bends its shaft: Behold Khufaf, that I am dhalika (this one)."

Meaning: I am this one.

We have clarified this topic and mentioned its aspects in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab), at the beginning of surah "al-Baqarah". And His saying: "natluhā" means "naqra'uhā" (We recite it) to you.

He, exalted is He, attributed its recitation to Himself, because it is His speech which He sent down to His Messenger through the angel, and He commanded the angel to recite it to him, conveying from Him, exalted is He.

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾ ﴿So when We have recited it, follow its recitation﴾ ﴿Then upon Us is its explanation﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16-19].

So His saying "fa-idha qara'nahu" means: when the angel sent with it from Our side recited it to you, conveying from Us, and you heard it from him, "fa-ittaba' Qur'anahu" means: follow its recitation and recite it as you heard him reciting it.

He, exalted is He, has also pointed to this in His saying: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾ [Taha: 114].

His ﷺ hearing the Qur'an from the angel who conveyed from Allah the speech of Allah, and his understanding of it, is the meaning of its being sent down (p-187) upon his heart, in His saying: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then indeed he has sent it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 97].

• And His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ ﴿upon your heart, that you may be of the warners﴾ ﴿in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192-195].

• And His saying in this verse: ﴿These are the signs of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6],

meaning His legislated religious signs.

Know that the word "ayah" is used in the Arabic language in two senses, and in the Great Qur'an in two senses as well.

As for its usage in the Arabic language:

The first of them, which is the well-known one in the speech of the Arabs, is its use in the sense of "sign" (dalil/'alamah). This is widespread in Arabic speech, and from it is the saying of Nabighah Dhubyani:

"I recognized the traces of its signs after six years, and this year is the seventh."

Then he clarified that his intended meaning by "signs" was the markers of the abode in his saying after it:

"Ashes like the kohl of the eye, I clarify its traces, and a pit like the base of a pool, its edge worn down and humbled."

As for the second of them, it is the use of "ayah" in the sense of "group": they say, "The people came with their ayah," i.e., with their group.

From it is the saying of Burj ibn Musahhir:

"We went out from the two passes, there is no tribe like ours, with our ayah we drive the milch camels with their young."

His saying "bi-ayatina" means "with our group."

As for its usage in the Great Qur'an: the first of them is its use for the legislated religious sign, like the signs of this Great Qur'an, and from it is His saying here: ﴿These are the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾, and so on.

As for the second: it is its use for the cosmic, predestined sign, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, are signs for people of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190].

The cosmic predestined sign is in the meaning of the linguistic sign which is the indication, because the cosmic signs are decisive indicators that their Creator is the Lord who alone is worshipped.

(p-188) As for the legislated religious sign, some scholars said: it too is of the sense of "ayah" meaning sign, because the signs of this Great Qur'an are indications of the truthfulness of the one who brought them, by what they contain of the proof of inimitability, or because in them are indications by which the beginning and end of the verses are known.

Some scholars said: it is of the sense of "ayah" meaning group, because it includes a whole group and collection of the words and letters of the Qur'an.

Many have chosen that the original form of "ayah" is "ayyah" (with a fatha on the hamza and fathas on the two yas after it), so the two yas came together, both requiring i'lal (weakening change); because each of them is vowelled with an original vowel after a connected fatha, as he indicated in the Khulasah (Ibn Malik's Alfiyya) with his saying:

"A waw or ya vowelled by an original vowel, after a connected fatha, is changed to alif."

"If the following one is vowelled..." etc.

It is known in the science of morphology (tasrif) that if two causes of i'lal come together in one word, the more common practice in the Arabic language is to keep the first of them sound and to weaken the second by changing it to alif, like al-hawa, al-nawa, al-tawa, al-shawa. Perhaps the second is kept sound and the first is weakened, like ghayah, rayah, and ayah, according to the most correct of many opinions. It is known that weakening both of them is not valid, and for this he indicated in the Khulasah with his saying:

"If the weakening is due for two letters, one is kept sound, and the reverse may also be due."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ ﴿who hears the signs of Allah recited to him, then persists in arrogance as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾.

What He, exalted is He, mentioned in this noble verse, that whoever disbelieves in Allah and in the signs of Allah, and does not believe in that despite the manifestation of the proofs and evidences that belief in Allah and His signs is obligatory, it is unlikely that he will believe in anything else; for if he believed in a statement, he would have believed in Allah and His signs, because the proofs of that are manifest. And that whoever does not believe in the signs of Allah is threatened with woe, and that he is a sinful liar. The "afFak" is one who frequently lies, and it is the worst kind of lying; and the "athim" is one who commits sin with his heart and limbs; he is a criminal in his heart, tongue and limbs. He, exalted is He, has mentioned this in other places, and He threatened those who deny this Qur'an with woe on the Day of Resurrection, and He clarified the unlikelihood of their belief in "what statement" after they did not believe in this Qur'an, and that is by His saying at the end of "al-Mursalat": (p-189) ﴿And when it is said to them: Bow down, they do not bow down﴾ ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ [al-Mursalat: 48-50]. So His saying: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ is like His saying here: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾.

He, exalted is He, has repeated the threat of woe to the deniers in Surah "al-Mursalat," as is well known, and His saying at the end of "al-Mursalat": ﴿Then in what statement after it will they believe?﴾ is like His saying here in "al-Jathiyah": ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾.

It is known that belief in Allah in its correct form necessitates belief in His signs, and belief in His signs likewise necessitates belief in Him, exalted is He. His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿who hears the signs of Allah recited to him, then persists in arrogance as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ indicates that whoever hears the Qur'an recited, then persists in disbelief and sins while being arrogant toward submitting to the truth contained in the verses of the Qur'an, as if he had not heard the signs of Allah, for him is the tidings on the Day of Resurrection of a painful punishment, which is abiding forever in the Fire. What this noble verse contains has come clarified in other places,

- such as His saying, exalted is He, in "Luqman": ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in arrogance as though he had not heard them, as though there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a punishment﴾ [Luqman: 7].

- And His saying, exalted is He, in "al-Hajj": ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve; they nearly attack those who recite Our verses to them. Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieved; and wretched is the destination﴾ [al-Hajj: 72].

- And His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave you they say to those who were given knowledge: What did he just say? Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and who follow their desires﴾ [Muhammad: 16].

His saying about them, exalted is He: "What did he just say?" indicates that they did not care about what the Prophet ﷺ recited to them of the verses and guidance.

We have mentioned many of the verses related to this topic in Surah "Fussilat" in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾ ﴿And they say: Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you call us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so act﴾ [Fussilat: 4-5].

His saying, exalted is He, in this verse: ﴿as though he had not heard them﴾, the word "ka'anna" has been lightened (made light, kaʼan). It is known that when "ka'anna" is lightened, its noun is implied, and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), and the clause is its predicate, as he said in the Khulasah: (p-190)

"And ka'anna is also lightened; its object is implied, and it is also reported to be stated."

We have already mentioned at the beginning of Surah "al-Kahf" that "bishara" (tidings) is generally used for the report of what pleases, and that it is sometimes used in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech for the report of what displeases as well. We clarified that with its Arabic evidences. His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾, some scholars said: "Woe" is a valley in Hell.

The more apparent view is that the word "woe" (waylun) is a word of punishment and destruction, that it is a verbal noun with no verb of its own derivation, and that what makes it permissible to begin with it, although it is indefinite, is that it occurs in the context of invoking destruction upon them.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾

It was recited by Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Hafs from 'Asim: "yu'minun" with the ya' of the third person.

It was recited by Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Shu'bah from 'Asim: "tu'minun" with the ta' of address.

It was recited by Warsh from Nafi', and al-Susi from Abu 'Amr: "yumanun," with the hamza changed to waw, both in connection and in pause.

Hamzah recited it with the hamza changed to waw in pause only, not in connection.

The rest recited it with the hamza realized fully in all cases.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 9:

Allah's saying: ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule. For such there is a humiliating punishment.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions the threat of woe to the lying sinner, and the good tidings of a painful punishment.

We have already mentioned shortly that among his characteristics is that when the verses of Allah are recited to him, he persists in arrogance as if he had not heard them. In this noble verse He mentions that when he learns anything of the verses of Allah, he takes them in ridicule, i.e., made into a mockery, treating them lightly, and then He threatens him for that with a humiliating punishment.

What this noble verse includes, that the disbelievers take the verses of Allah in ridicule and that they will be punished for that on the Day of Resurrection, Allah has explained in other places,

- like His saying, Exalted is He, at the end of surah "al-Kahf": ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in ridicule.﴾ [al-Kahf: 106].

- and His saying, Exalted is He, also in "al-Kahf": ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth, and they take My verses and that with which they are warned in ridicule.﴾ ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth?﴾ — to the end of the verse [al-Kahf: 56–57].

- and His saying in surah "al-Jathiyah" here: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day, and your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ ﴿That is because you took the verses of Allah in ridicule.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34–35].

The seven readers, except Hamzah and Hafs from Asim, recited this letter-group as هُزُؤًا, with a damma on the zay and after it a clearly articulated hamzah.

Hafs from Asim recited it with a damma on the zay and replacing the hamzah with a waw.

Hamzah recited it as هُزْءًا, with a sukun on the zay and after it a clearly articulated hamzah in pause-less connection (wasl).

As for pausing (waqf), there is from Hamzah the transfer of the hamzah's vowel to the zay, so the zay becomes fatha followed by an alif, and from him also its replacement by a waw vowelled with the vowel of the hamzah.

His saying, Exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿For such there is a humiliating punishment﴾ means that the punishment of the disbelievers who used to mock the verses of Allah is intended only as their humiliation, their disgrace, and the severe infliction of pain upon them with various kinds of punishment.

There is in it no purification or expiation for them, unlike the disobedient among the Muslims, for they, though they are punished, will enter Paradise after that punishment.

So the purpose of their punishment is not mere humiliation; rather, after it they will return to mercy and the abode of honour.

The Exalted said: "Before them is Hell, and what they earned will not avail them at all, nor those they took as protectors besides Allah. And for them is a great punishment."

The Exalted said: "Before them is Hell." We have already set forth the verses that clarify this, together with the Arabic evidences, in Surat Ibrahim, in the discussion of the Exalted's words: "And they sought victory, and every obstinate tyrant was disappointed. Before him is Hell" [Ibrahim: 15–16]. There we explained that the more correct of the two views is that (wara') here means "in front of" (amam).

So the meaning of "from behind them, Hell" is: in front of them is Hell, which they will burn in on the Day of Resurrection, as the Exalted said: "And behind them was a king who seized every boat by force" [al-Kahf: 79], meaning: in front of them was a king.

We mentioned there the Arabic evidences for the use of (wara') in the sense of (amam), and we explained that this is the verified meaning of the verse. The same applies to this verse of al-Jathiyah. Thus the Exalted's words "from behind them, Hell" mean: in front of them is Hell, which they will burn in on the Day of Resurrection.

As for the Exalted's words in this noble verse: "Nor will what they earned avail them at all, nor those they took as protectors besides Allah."

In it He makes clear that what the disbelievers gained in the worldly life, of wealth and children, will not avail them anything on the Day of Resurrection; that is, it will not benefit them in any way. No benefit will be brought to them through it, and no harm will be averted from them through it. As for those they took as protectors in the worldly life besides Allah, such as the objects of worship that they worshipped and claimed to be partners of Allah, these will not benefit them on the Day of Resurrection either.

These two matters contained in this noble verse have been made clear by Allah in many verses of His Book.

As for the first of them, namely that what they earned will not avail them, He has made it clear in many verses, such as:

• The Exalted's words: "Ruined are the two hands of Abu Lahab, and ruined is he. His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned" [al-Masad: 1–2].

• His words: "And his wealth will not avail him when he falls [into Hell]" [al-Layl: 11].

• His words: "Who gathered wealth and counted it, thinking his wealth would make him immortal. No! He will surely be thrown into the Crushing" [al-Humazah: 2–4].

• His words: "Those before them had said the same, but what they earned did not avail them" [al-Zumar: 50].

• His words: "Would that it had been the end. My wealth has not availed me" [al-Haqqah: 27–28].

• His words: "They will say: What your gathering and your arrogance availed you not" [al-A'raf: 48].

• His words about Ibrahim: "And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected, the Day when neither wealth nor children will benefit" [al-Shu'ara': 87–88].

• His words: "It is not your wealth or your children that will bring you near to Us in rank" [Saba': 37].

• His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all, and they are the fuel of the Fire" [Al 'Imran: 10].

• His words: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all, and they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever" [Al 'Imran: 116].

• His words in "al-Mujadilah": "They took their oaths as a shield, and barred others from the way of Allah, so for them is a humiliating punishment. Their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all" [al-Mujadilah: 16–17].

Verses of this kind are very numerous, and we have presented many of them in various places of this blessed Book.

As for the second matter, namely that the objects they took as protectors besides Allah will not benefit them, He, the Exalted, has made it clear in many verses,

• such as His words in "Hud": "We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. The gods they invoked besides Allah did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came, and they added nothing but ruin" [Hud: 101].

• His words: "Why did those they had taken as gods besides Allah, as means of approach, not help them? Rather they went astray from them, and that was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate" [al-Ahqaf: 28].

• His words: "And it will be said: Call your partners, so they will call them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided" [al-Qasas: 64].

• His words: "And on the Day He says: Call My partners whom you claimed, so they will call them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction" [al-Kahf: 52].

• His words: "And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them" [al-Ahqaf: 5–6].

• His words: "That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a speck. If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association" [Fatir: 13–14].

• His words: "And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be for them a source of might. No! They will reject their worship of them and will be opposed to them" [Maryam: 81–82].

• His words: "And he said: You have taken idols besides Allah only as a bond of affection among you in the worldly life; then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disown others and curse one another, and your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers" [al-'Ankabut: 25].

As for the Exalted's words in this noble verse: "Nor those they took as protectors besides Allah." The awliya' (protectors) is the plural of wali.

What is meant by the awliya' here is the objects of worship to which they allied themselves through worship besides Allah. The "ma" in His words "what they earned" and "what they took" is a relative pronoun, and it is in the nominative position in both places: the first "ma" is the subject of yughni (avails), and the second "ma" is coordinated with it. The insertion of "la" before a coordinated element after a negated verb is well known.

His words "yughni" mean: "yanfa'" (benefit). The apparent origin of it is from ghana' (with fatha and a long vowel), which is benefit.

From it is the words of the poet:

"Little benefit to you is the wealth you gathered when it becomes inheritance and the grave conceals you."

So his words "qalla ghana'" mean: "little benefit." And the words of another:

"Benefit has diminished when a youth meets destruction, the words of loved ones: do not be far, though they have departed."

So his words "al-ghana'" mean "benefit."

This verse is among the evidences for the governing action of the verbal noun defined by al-alif wa-al-lam, because His words "qawlu al-ahibbah" (the words of the beloveds) are the subject of "al-ghana'." As for ghina' (with kasra and a long vowel), it means melodious singing.

As for ghina (with kasra and short vowel), it means the opposite of poverty.

As for ghana (with fatha and short vowel), it means residing, from the saying: "ghaniya bi-al-makan" (with kasra on the nun), "yaghna" (with fatha), "ghana" (with two fathas), when one resides in it.

From it is the Exalted's words: "As if it had not flourished yesterday" [Yunus: 24], and His words: "As if they had never dwelt therein" [al-A'raf: 92], meaning as if they had never lived there.

As for ghunna (with damma and short vowel), it is the plural of ghunya, which is that by which a person becomes self-sufficient.

As for ghunā' (with damma and long vowel), I do not know it in Arabic.

These dialectal forms that we have mentioned under the root gh-n-y I received at the beginning of my youth in a lesson of jurisprudence taught to me by my great teacher Ahmad al-Afram ibn Muhammad al-Mukhtar al-Jakani, who also recited to me two verses of rajaz on this matter by one of the eminent scholars of the region, which are:

"The opposite of poverty, like ila, and like suhab: benefit; and the one who gladdens, likewise like kitab.

And like fata, residence; and like huna, the plural of ghunya, is what makes one self-sufficient."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is guidance. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord — for them is a painful punishment of wretched torment.﴾

The demonstrative in His saying ﴿This is guidance﴾ refers to the Great Qur'an, which is expressed by the signs of Allah in His saying ﴿These are the signs of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 6].

• And His saying: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Jathiyah: 6].

• And His saying: ﴿He hears the signs of Allah recited to him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 8].

• And His saying: ﴿And when he learns something of Our signs﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 9].

What this noble verse includes, that this Qur'an is guidance, and that whoever disbelieves in its signs has the painful punishment, has come clarified in other places.

As for the Qur'an being guidance, He, exalted, mentioned it in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [al-A'raf: 52].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims﴾ [al-Nahl: 89].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿The month of Ramadan in which the Qur'an was revealed as guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

• And His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 1-2].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

The verses similar to these are many and well known.

As for the one who disbelieves in the Qur'an incurring, because of that, the painful punishment, it has come clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted: ﴿And whoever of the sects disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place. So be not in doubt about it﴾ up to the end of the verse [Hud: 17].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder. Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden, abiding therein; and evil is their burden on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Ta-Ha: 99-101].

• And His saying, exalted: ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, for what they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in ridicule﴾ [al-Kahf: 106].

The verses similar to this are many and well known.

We have already discussed, in the surah of "Fussilat", His saying, exalted: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾ up to the end of the verse [Fussilat: 17], and elsewhere, that guidance is used in the Qur'an in a general sense, meaning that guidance is clarification, direction, and making the truth manifest,

• like His saying: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾, i.e., We made the truth clear to them and manifested it, and directed them to it, even though they did not follow it,

• and like His saying: ﴿a guidance for the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

• And His saying here: ﴿This is guidance.﴾ It is also used in the Qur'an in its specific meaning, which is the bestowal of grace in guiding to the path of truth and election,

• like His saying: ﴿a guidance for the righteous﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2].

• And His saying: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

• And His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

• And His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90].

Up to other verses besides these.

We have made clear in the surah of "Fussilat" that knowing the usage of the two kinds of guidance mentioned removes the difficulty found in verses of the Book of Allah.

Huda (guidance) is a verbal noun (masdar) of hadahu, irregularly formed, and here it is of the type of describing by the verbal noun. We have explained earlier, many times, that treating a verbal noun as an adjective is either by omitting an annexed noun (mudaf) or by hyperbole.

On the first view, the meaning is: this Qur'an possesses guidance, i.e., guidance is attained through it for whoever follows it, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9].

On the second view, the meaning is that the intent is hyperbole in the Qur'an's attribute of guidance, to the point that it is said of it that it is itself guidance.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿For them is a painful punishment of wretched torment (min rijzin alim)﴾, the more correct of the two views concerning it is that rijz here means punishment, and there is no repetition in the verse, because punishment has various kinds that differ; the meaning is: for them is a punishment of the same kind as the painful punishment, and alim means painful (mu'lim), i.e., characterized by intensity of pain and its severity.

And the verified view, Allah willing, is that the Arabs use the form fa'il as an adjective in the sense of muf'il. What is reported from al-Asma'i, that he denied this, if it is correctly ascribed to him, is an error on his part, because the use of fa'il in the sense of muf'il is well known in the Great Qur'an and in Arabic speech. From its use in the Great Qur'an is His saying, exalted: ﴿a painful punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 104], i.e., painful (mu'lim); and His saying, exalted: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 117], i.e., the one who originates them; and His saying, exalted: ﴿He is only a warner to you﴾ up to the end of the verse [Saba': 46], i.e., one who warns you. A parallel in Arabic speech is the saying of Amr ibn Ma'd Yakrib:

"Is it from Rayhana, the summoning one who hears, that I am kept awake, while my companions sleep?"

So his saying "al-da'i al-sami'" means the summoner who makes [others] hear. And his saying also:

"And a cavalry that you approached with a horse of... their greeting among them is a striking and a painful blow."

i.e., painful (mu'lim). And the saying of Ghaylan ibn Uqbah:

"And there rises from chests of... that strike their faces a painful blaze."

i.e., painful (mu'lim). And all the seven readers except Ibn Kathir and Hafs from Asim read this letter: ﴿min rijzin alimin﴾ with the genitive alimin, as an attribute of rijz. Ibn Kathir and Hafs from Asim read: min rijzin alimun, with the nominative alimun, as an attribute of adhab.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is Allah who subjected the sea to you, that ships may sail upon it by His command, and that you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-Nahl" (The Bee), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 14]. And in Surah "al-Zukhruf" (The Ornaments of Gold), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And the One who created all the pairs﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and we were not able to subdue them﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 12-13].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self, and whoever does evil, it is against it.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il" (The Children of Israel), in the discussion of His saying: ﴿If you do good, you do good for your own souls﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Isra': 7]. And in other places besides these.

**The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 45, verse 16:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We preferred them over the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 16].

In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentions that He preferred the Children of Israel over the worlds, and He mentions this meaning in another place in His Book,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat "al-Baqarah": ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 47 - 122] in both places.

• And His saying in "ad-Dukhan": ﴿And We chose them knowingly over the worlds﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 32].

• And His saying in "al-A'raf": ﴿He said, "Should I seek for you a god other than Allah while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 140].

However, Allah - majestic and exalted - has made clear that the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) is better than the Children of Israel and more honored by Allah, as He stated explicitly in His saying: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind, enjoining what is right﴾ - the verse (p-198) [Aal 'Imran: 110]. So "khayr" (best) is a form of comparative superlative, and the verse is a clear text that they are better than all the nations, the Children of Israel and others.

What further clarifies this is the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri - may Allah be pleased with him - that the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning his Ummah: "You are completing seventy nations; you are the best of them and the most honored of them before Allah." It was narrated from him by Imam Ahmad, at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Hakim, and it is a well-known hadith.

Ibn Kathir said: at-Tirmidhi graded it hasan, and something similar is narrated from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa'id.

The author of these notes - may Allah pardon him and forgive him - says: There is no doubt about the soundness of the meaning of the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah mentioned - may Allah be pleased with him - because it is supported by the infallible, mutawatir text in His saying: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 110]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. His saying "wasatan" means: best and just.

Know that what we have mentioned regarding the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) being superior to the Children of Israel, as the mentioned verse and hadith and others of the evidences indicate, does not contradict the verses mentioned above about the preference of the Children of Israel.

Because that preference mentioned regarding the Children of Israel was stated concerning them in the state of the non-existence of the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

And what is non-existent in its non-existence is not a thing so that it can be preferred or be preferred over.

Rather, after the existence of the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), He, may He be exalted, explicitly stated that it is the best of the nations.

This is clear; because everything that came in the Qur'an about the preference of the Children of Israel only intends the mention of past conditions.

Because at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an they disbelieved in it and denied it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89].

It is known that Allah did not mention to them in the Qur'an any virtue except what is intended to be in their former time, not at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an.

And it is known that the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) did not exist in that former time, which is the period (p-199) of the preference of the Children of Israel; and that after its existence, Allah explicitly stated that it is the best of the nations, as we have clarified. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We placed you on a clear way of the affair, so follow it﴾.

We have already presented the clarifying verses in surah "al-Zukhruf" in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So hold fast to that which has been revealed to you; indeed you are on a straight path﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 43].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted is He, forbade His Prophet ﷺ from following the desires of those who do not know.

We have already presented, in surah "Bani Isra'il", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit reproved and forsaken﴾ [al-Isra': 22], that He, majestic and exalted, commands His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and forbids him, so that by that command and prohibition He legislates for his community, as in His saying here: ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 18].

It is known that he ﷺ does not follow the desires of those who do not know, but the prohibition mentioned in it is legislation for his community,

• like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾ [al-Insan: 24];

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not obey the deniers﴾ [al-Qalam: 8];

• and His saying: ﴿And do not obey every swearer, despicable one﴾ [al-Qalam: 10];

• and His saying: ﴿And do not set up with Allah another god﴾ [al-Isra': 39];

• and His saying: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65].

Verses of this kind are many.

We have already shown the Qur'anic evidences that he ﷺ is addressed while the intended meaning is legislation for his community, in the verse of "Bani Isra'il" mentioned above.

What the verse of "al-Jathiyah" contains of the prohibition against following their desires has come clarified in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted, in "al-Shura": ﴿And do not follow their desires, and say: I believe in what Allah has sent down of a Book﴾ [al-Shura: 15]. And His saying, may He be exalted, in "al-An'am": ﴿So if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 150]. And His saying, may He be exalted, in "al-Qasas": ﴿But if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Qasas: 50]. Verses of this kind are many and well known.

(p-200) Allah, exalted is He, has clarified in ﴿Successful indeed are the believers﴾ that if the truth had followed their desires, the world would have been corrupted; and that is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 71].

Al-ahwa' (the desires) is the plural of hawa (desire), with two fatahs, and its origin is a verbal noun; the hamzah in it is substituted from a ya', as is well known.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 19:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾.

We have already mentioned in this blessed book, many times, that *zulm* (wrongdoing) in the language of the Arabs is originally the placing of a thing in other than its proper place.

The greatest kind of it is *shirk* (associating partners with Allah), because directing worship to other than the One who created and provides is the most heinous kind of placing a thing in other than its proper place.

For this reason, the term *zulm* is frequently used in the Great Qur'an to mean *shirk*,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 254].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not call upon, besides Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way"﴾ [Al-Furqan: 27].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Luqman: ﴿O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association with Him is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. It is established in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Prophet (ﷺ) explained His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ [Al-An'am: 82], that its meaning is: "and did not mix their belief with *shirk*."

What is contained in this verse of "Al-Jathiyah," that the wrongdoers are allies of one another, has been mentioned in other places as well,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of "Al-Anfal": ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do this, there will be fitnah (turmoil) in the land and great corruption﴾ [Al-Anfal: 73].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾ [Al-An'am: 129].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their allies are the taghut (false objects of worship). They bring them out of the light into darkness﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies besides Allah﴾, the verse [7].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾, the verse [An-Nisa': 76].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is only Satan frightening his allies﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175].

• And His saying: (p-201) ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾, the verse [An-Nahl: 100].

Besides these, there are other verses.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is the ally of the righteous﴾.

He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse that He is the Ally of the *muttaqun* (the God-fearing), who are those who carry out His command and avoid His prohibitions.

He mentioned in another place that the God-fearing are His allies. Thus He is their Ally, and they are His allies, because they show loyalty to Him through obedience and faith, and He shows them loyalty through mercy and reward. This is in His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, the allies of Allah – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾.

Then He clarified who is meant by His allies in His saying: ﴿Those who believed and were fearing Allah﴾ [Yunus: 63]. His saying, "and were fearing Allah," is like His saying in this verse of "Al-Jathiyah": ﴿And Allah is the ally of the God-fearing﴾.

Allah, may He be exalted, has also explained in verses of His Book that He is the Ally of the believers and that they are His allies,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your ally is only Allah and His Messenger﴾, the verse [Al-Ma'idah: 55].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is because Allah is the protector of those who believe﴾, the verse [Muhammad: 11].

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, my ally is Allah, who revealed the Book, and He is an ally of the righteous﴾ [Al-A'raf: 196].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, concerning the angels: ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our ally, not them"﴾, the verse [Saba': 41].

Besides these, there are other verses, as has been explained in more detail above than this.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is insights for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who are certain.﴾

The demonstrative in His saying "this" refers to the Mighty Qur'an.

"Basair" (insights) is the plural of "basirah" (insight), and what is meant by it is the decisive proof that leaves no confusion regarding the truth, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "This is my way; I call to Allah upon insight"﴾ [Yusuf: 108], i.e., upon knowledge and clear evidence.

The meaning is that this Qur'an is decisive proofs and shining evidences that Allah alone is the one worshipped, and that what Muhammad ﷺ brought is the truth.

What this noble verse includes, that the Qur'an is insights for mankind, has been explained in other places in the Book of Allah, like His saying, may He be exalted, at the end of "al-A'raf" (p-202): ﴿Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. These are insights from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe."﴾ [al-A'raf: 203]. And His saying in "al-An'am": ﴿There has certainly come to you insights from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul; and whoever is blind, it is against it; and I am not over you a guardian.﴾ [al-An'am: 104].

What the verse of "al-Jathiyah" includes, that the Qur'an is insights, guidance and mercy, He, may He be exalted, mentioned the like of it in surah "al-Qasas" about the Book of Musa, which is the Torah, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the Book after We had destroyed the former generations as insights for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, that they might remember.﴾ [al-Qasas: 43].

What this verse of "al-Jathiyah" includes, that the Qur'an is guidance and mercy, has been explained in other than this place.

As for its being guidance, we have mentioned the verses that explain it shortly before.

As for its being mercy, we have mentioned the verses that explain it in "al-Kahf" in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they found a servant from among Our servants whom We had given mercy from Us﴾ [al-Kahf: 65]. And at its beginning, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has sent down to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1]. And in "Fatir", in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whatever Allah grants to the people of mercy, none can withhold it﴾ [Fatir: 2]. And in "al-Zukhruf", in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ and the verse that follows [al-Zukhruf: 32].

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿for a people who are certain﴾, i.e., because they are the ones who benefit from it.

In this noble verse there is a well-known Arabic question: the subject, which is His saying "this", is a demonstrative pronoun referring to a singular masculine noun, while the predicate, which is "basair", is a broken feminine plural.

It is asked: how is a broken feminine plural attributed to a singular masculine? The answer: the whole of the Qur'an is one book, and the demonstrative may refer to it with this, and this one book comprises many proofs, so the attribution of "basair" to it is correct, because it includes them, as is not hidden.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 21:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them equal to those who believe and do righteous deeds?﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah Sad (38), in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: (p-203) ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We make the pious like the wicked?﴾ [Sad 38:28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken as his god his own desire?﴾.

We have already clarified its meaning in Surah "al-Furqan" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen one who has taken as his god his own desire? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ [al-Furqan: 43].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He has sealed over his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a veil.﴾

We have already clarified its meaning in Surah "al-Baqarah" in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has sealed over their hearts and over their hearing, and over their sights is a veil﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and we live."﴾

What this noble verse contains of the disbelievers' denial of resurrection (al-ba'th) after death has been made clear in many verses, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He, concerning them: ﴿And we will not be resurrected.﴾ [al-Dukhan: 35]

• And His saying: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought out? Far, far is what you are promised. There is not but our worldly life; we die and we live, and we will not be resurrected.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 35–37]

• And His saying, exalted is He, concerning them: ﴿When we have died and become dust, that is a far return.﴾ [Qaf: 3]

• And His saying, exalted is He, concerning them: ﴿Are we indeed to be returned to our former state? Even when we have become decayed bones?﴾ ﴿They said, "That would then be a losing return."﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 10–12]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]

The verses of this kind are many and well known.

We have already presented the decisive Qur'anic proofs refuting their denial of resurrection, and we explained their indication that resurrection is certainly going to happen, in Surat al-Baqarah, Surat al-Nahl, Surat al-Hajj, and at the beginning of this Surat al-Jathiyah, and we have referred to that many times.

In Surat al-Furqan we explained the verses that make clear that denying resurrection is disbelief in Allah, and the verses in which the threat of the Fire is directed at those who deny resurrection, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾ [al-Furqan: 11] (p. 204)

The Exalted said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day the falsifiers will be lost.﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah "al-Mu'min" (Ghafir), in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when the command of Allah comes, it will be decided in truth, and the falsifiers will be lost therein at that time.﴾ [Ghafir: 78].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 28:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record﴾ — the verse.

We have already explained it in Surah "al-Kahf" in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is Our Record; it speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in surah Maryam, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, We will record what he says and extend for him of punishment an extension﴾ [Maryam: 79], and in other places.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day."﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be given the chance to make amends.﴾

We have already clarified the meaning of His saying, yusta'tabun (they will be given the chance to make amends), in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness; then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be allowed to make amends.﴾ [an-Nahl: 84].

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it﴾, we have previously presented the verses that explain it in Surat az-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain [in torment]."﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 77].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 36:

Allah's words: ﴿So all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, follows His praise by describing Himself as the Lord of the heavens and the earth and the Lord of the worlds (p-205). This indicates that the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and the Lord of the worlds, deserves every praise and every beautiful commendation.

What this noble verse contains is clarified in other verses, such as:

• His words in Surat "al-Fatihah": ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2].

• His words at the end of "az-Zumar": ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ [az-Zumar: 75].

• His words: ﴿So the people who did wrong were cut off, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-An'am: 45].

• His words at the beginning of "al-An'am": ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light.﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

• His words at the beginning of "Saba'": ﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him is praise in the Hereafter, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ [Saba': 1].

• His words at the beginning of "Fatir": ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth,﴾ ...the verse [Fatir: 1].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 45, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur (al-kibriya') in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that to Him belongs al-kibriya' (grandeur) in the heavens and the earth. It means that He alone is singled out for greatness, perfection, majesty and sovereignty in the heavens and the earth, because He is the one worshipped by the people of the heavens and the earth, the one whom they must magnify, glorify, exalt, and submit to and humble themselves before.

What this noble verse includes is explained in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth, and He is the Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ and ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 84-85].

His saying: ﴿He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾ means that He alone is the one who is magnified and worshipped in the heavens and the earth, and is glorified, submitted to and humbled before.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest description (al-mathal al-a'la) in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the Wise﴾ [ar-Rum: 27].

His saying: ﴿And to Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth﴾ means that to Him belongs the most perfect attribute, which is the greatest, most complete and most sublime of attributes, in the heavens and the earth.

In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Indeed Allah says: Greatness is My waist-wrapper (izar) and grandeur is My cloak (rida'), so whoever disputes with Me over either of them, I will cast him into My Fire."
